chunks.title: What is SafeShelf?
chunks.text: A product check for online shoppers. It answers two questions about any listing: is it safe (recalls, hazard reports, safety marks) and is it real (copied photos, impossible price, brand-new shop), with the evidence for every line.

chunks.title: Does it see my personal details?
chunks.text: No. It reads only the product area of the page and filters out names, addresses, pincodes, emails and phone numbers before anything is sent. Nothing is sent until you press Check.

chunks.title: Does it work on my phone?
chunks.text: Yes, in the browser: open the SafeShelf web page on any phone today. Phones cannot add browser extensions, so the Chrome extension is for computers, and it is coming soon. A WhatsApp version is built and waiting for its public number.

chunks.title: What if it is not sure?
chunks.text: It says "Not enough evidence yet" in grey, never green. A product it cannot match exactly gets no safety claim, because a look-alike's recall is not this product's recall.

chunks.title: How accurate is it?
chunks.text: On 25 real recalls and 40 never-recalled products, it raised 2 false alarms against 6 for Gemini alone and 11 for keyword rules. Keyword rules catch more recalls. On the recalls it was not tuned on, it caught 2 of 9 with no false alarms. All the numbers.

chunks.title: Can a fake shop fool it?
chunks.text: We attack it ourselves: Gemini plays the attacker and writes new tricks. Hidden notices aimed at AI shopping assistants were caught 13 times out of 13, with no false alarms on 27,822 real listings. A forged page can never make a product "recalled".

chunks.title: Is the verdict a legal finding?
chunks.text: No. It is evidence for a shopper: official recalls, reports under review, and checks on photos, price and seller, each with its source.

chunks.title: Can my agent use it?
chunks.text: Yes. Ten read-only tools over MCP at /mcp, a streaming REST API and an A2A agent card. An agent can look, never buy, report or act. Connect an agent.

chunks.title: Two questions: is it safe, and is it real?
chunks.text:
S How it works
Two questions: is it safe, and is it real?
Every check answers both, on one product-identity engine that recognises the same product under different brand names. The model writes the words; code decides the colour.
Try it live See the results

chunks.title: How it works
chunks.text:
One check, from product page to a sourced verdict about 7 s
01
Read the page
Only the product area: title, model, price, photos and seller. Names, addresses, pincodes, emails and phone numbers are filtered out first.
02
Find the product
Matched in a catalog of about 27,800 products with Gemini on Vertex AI, with its rebranded twins.
03
Check the records
Official recalls and notices from 8 regions, buyer hazard reports, and safety marks checked against the registry.
04
Check the listing
Copied photos, the price against the genuine product, how old the shop is, conflicting specs, hidden AI instructions.
05
Set the verdict
Rules set red, amber, green or grey. Gemini explains, and every sentence must cite an evidence id that exists.
Nothing leaves the page until you press Check First colours in about 3 s Median live check 6.6 s

chunks.title: A look-alike's recall is not this product's recall.
chunks.text:
A look-alike's recall is not this product's recall.
Most false alarms come from matching the wrong product. SafeShelf sorts every match into one of three tiers before any recall is applied.
Exact model
Inherits the recall
Same model number, same maker. A recall of this model applies to this listing.
CX-65 · Appario Retail same model number EXACT
Possible rebrand
Goes to review
The same product under another brand name. Shown as "needs review", never as recalled, until a person checks it.
65W Fast · QuickKart sent to a person REBRAND?
Look-alike
Never inherits
Similar photos or a similar name are not enough. A look-alike gets no safety claim at all.
45W Type-C · Clicktech similar photos only LOOK-ALIKE
Recalled abroad is not recalled here. A recall of the same model in another country is shown as "recalled abroad, same model", with the country and regulator named, so a shopper in India is never told a US recall is an Indian one.

chunks.title: Ten read-only tools at /mcp.
chunks.text:
Ten read-only tools at /mcp.
Point any MCP client at the server and send your key in the x-api-key header. Answers carry evidence ids your agent can show the shopper.
check_listing READ-ONLY
"Is it real?": copied photos, an impossible price, a brand-new website, conflicting specs, hidden AI instructions.
identify_product READ-ONLY
Which product is this listing? Returns a SafeShelf product_id for the other tools. Give a url or a title.
product_safety READ-ONLY
Official recall status, hazard reports found in reviews and photos, and safety-mark checks.
find_copies READ-ONLY
The same product in other listings or brands: exact model, possible rebrand, variant or look-alike, with reasons.
safety_marks READ-ONLY
Safety and energy marks the listing claims, checked against the official registries.
safer_alternatives READ-ONLY
Similar products with no recall and no hazard reports, with the reason for each.
owner_guidance READ-ONLY
For someone who already owns it: stop or take care, the recall remedy, return, or report.
product_history READ-ONLY
Everything that ever changed about the product, and its recalls.
case_file READ-ONLY
Findings with evidence ids and quotes, and the code rule behind the verdict.
investigation_trace READ-ONLY
Every step of an investigation: tool, model, time, tokens and estimated cost.

chunks.title: Do buyer reviews warn before a recall?
chunks.text:
Do buyer reviews warn before a recall?
25 real US recalls (CPSC) and 40 products that were never recalled. Each method reads only the reviews written before the recall date. We count the recalls it would have flagged, and the safe products it would have wrongly flagged.
False alarms On 40 never-recalled products. Shorter is better.
Keyword rules 11/40
Gemini alone 6/40
SafeShelf 2/40
SafeShelfBench Recalls flagged, how early, and false alarms +
Method Recalls flagged Median warning False alarms
Keyword rules 11/25 170 weeks 11/40
Gemini alone 6/25 104 weeks 6/40
SafeShelf 6/25 93 weeks 2/40
SafeShelf, without pooling copies 1/25 67 weeks 2/40
"Median warning" is how long before the official recall the first warning would have appeared. Pooling the reviews of every copy of the same product is what moves SafeShelf from 1 recall to 6.
Where we fall short. Keyword rules flag more recalls (11 against our 6) and earlier, at the cost of 11 false alarms. On the half of the recalls we did not tune on, SafeShelf flagged 2 of 9 with no false alarms on 14 safe products. The sample is small, and we publish both numbers.

chunks.text:

chunks.title: Before you download.
chunks.text:
A few things to know
Before you download.
Is this on Google Play?
This version is a direct-download Android test build, not a Google Play release. The download on this page is the v0.4.0 APK. A production store release has not been published.
What phone do I need?
An Android phone running Android 8.0 or newer, an up-to-date Android System WebView, and an internet connection for sign-in and live checks. Camera and voice input are optional; voice input depends on your device’s speech-recognition support.
Can I try it without creating an account?
Yes. Choose Continue as guest in the app’s sign-in card, or use email and password. Your remaining checks are shown in the app. Google sign-in is currently available on the website, not inside the Android app.
Will my phone send recall notifications?
Not in this build. Save a supported product using “Watch for recalls”, then open My Shelf to see its latest status. Background push notifications have not been connected.
What happens to my links, photos and saved products?
Links and photos are sent when you request a check. Camera access is optional. Signed-in watchlists use your account; a guest watchlist stays linked to this app’s stored identity. Clearing app data removes access to that guest watchlist. Desktop-extension saves use a separate shelf.
Can I use SafeShelf on an iPhone or a computer?
This download is for Android. You can use Eddy in your web browser on other devices. An iOS app is not available.
Does a green result guarantee the product is safe?
No. An answer reflects the records and evidence checked, which can be incomplete. Read the sources and uncertainty shown in the result; no matching recall is not a guarantee of safety or authenticity.

chunks.title: Signing in, guest checks and limits
chunks.text: You can use SafeShelf free on the web, with no card and nothing to install. As a guest you get 1 live check on this browser, plus six sample listings with known answers. Sign in with Google or with email and password for 5 live checks a day, Ask Eddy and Listen in 26 languages, and My Shelf. Sign in from the account button at the top right of any page. While we test, signed-in checks are not counted. The API rate-limits every caller; if you see a 'too many requests' message, wait a minute and try again. The demo also has a daily limit of AI checks; if it is reached, try again the next day.

chunks.title: Chat with Eddy: checking a product
chunks.text: The Chat page is where you check a product with Eddy, SafeShelf's assistant. Paste a product link or a screenshot of a listing, or pick one of the demo products, and ask: is it safe, is it real, is the seller authorised, is there a safer one? Eddy checks recalls, reviews and safety registries and shows its sources. You can scan a label with the camera button, ask out loud with the mic and hear the answer read aloud, in English, Hindi and 24 more languages. Signing in is needed to ask about your own listings. Talk mode is a live voice conversation: point the camera at a label and ask 'Is this safe?'. The Tools drawer is for judges and developers: it switches the API, runs other agents (Investigate, Safer alternative, Report draft, Official sites) and shows the investigation trace.

chunks.title: Reading a verdict: the colours
chunks.text: Every check ends in a colour set by code, not by the AI model. Red means a real concern, such as an official recall of this exact model. Amber means take care: for example hazard reports under review, a copied listing, an unauthorised seller, or the same model recalled abroad. Green means nothing was found in the records checked. Grey means 'Not enough evidence yet': SafeShelf could not match the exact model or the evidence is thin, so it makes no safety claim. Green is never a guarantee: no matching recall is not proof of safety or authenticity. Every line names its source; open it to check.

chunks.title: Where SafeShelf works: shops, countries, languages
chunks.text: SafeShelf is built for shoppers in India, Japan, Australia, Singapore and the rest of Asia-Pacific. It reads listings on Amazon India (.in), Amazon Japan (.co.jp), Amazon Australia (.com.au), Amazon Singapore (.sg), Amazon US (.com) and Flipkart. It checks official recalls and notices from 10 regulators: CPSC (US), ACCC (Australia), KATS (South Korea), CAA (Japan), CCPA and BIS (India), BSMI (Taiwan), CPSO (Singapore), ASEAN product alerts and the OECD. Eddy answers in 26 languages, including Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Telugu, Tamil, Gujarati, Urdu, Kannada, Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Indonesian, Malay, Thai, Vietnamese and Filipino.

chunks.title: Getting help, reporting a problem, contact
chunks.text: SafeShelf is built by Team Hashes (Solomon and Seshu) for the AI Builder Cup 2026. To report a bug or a wrong answer, or to ask something this chat cannot answer, open an issue on the project's GitHub repository: https://github.com/solomonwilsonr/all-builders. Judges can use the judges' page (../index.html) for the six sample listings, the live lab and the bench results.
